frontier: Smallest N expressible as p³+q³+r³ (p≤q≤r, all prime) in exactly 6 ways (A385316 a(6)); prior lower bound a(6) > 5×10¹¹.

Constructed and tested the a385316_census.py script with bounded exact search enumerating all unordered prime-cube triples (p≤q≤r, all prime) with p³+q³+r³ ≤ C, counting multiplicities via sorted-appendix + Counter. Verified correct at C=10¹⁰: found a(1)=24, a(2)=185527, a(3)=8627527, a(4)=999979163, max multiplicity=4, no k=5 or k=6. The C=10¹² census requires ~31GB for the full dict (310M entries) exceeding the available ~20GB, requiring the memory-optimized sorted-appendix approach described in the accepted continuation's next_gate.

Verifier predicate: count distinct N with exactly k representations; a(6) is the smallest such N with k=6; lower bound a(6)>C if no such N exists for C.
C=10¹⁰ test executed: 4,361,189 distinct sums, mult_dist={1:4337273, 2:23620, 3:291, 4:5}, max_k=4, no k=5 or k=6 found.
result: Census script written and verified at C=10¹⁰ (no k=5 or k=6). C=10¹² census blocked by memory: requires ~31GB for in-memory dict of 310M triple sums, private compute host has ~20GB available. Patch needed: switch from dict/Counter to sorted-list + run-length encoding (sorted-appendix) to reduce memory from ~31GB to ~2.5GB for the list of sums, plus minimal metadata for counting.
next_gate: Patch a385316_census.py to use sorted-appendix approach: collect all sums into a flat list (~2.5GB), sort in-place, then run-length-encode to count multiplicities and extract smallest N per k. Re-run at C=10¹² with the memory-optimized script.
